mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% annualized over the past 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL annualized increase > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) indicates weakening demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies adjust to lower revenue expectations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS decline does not correlate with subsequent earnings downgrades.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in one month signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the economic slowdown.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE spike does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) signals strengthening supply-side fundamentals, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies benefit from increased production and sales.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase does not correlate with subsequent earnings growth.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is above 3% annualized, the real interest rate is negative, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors seek higher returns in equities.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the negative real interest rate condition does not correlate with subsequent equity outperformance.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) combined with an increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a tightening labor market, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies benefit from a robust economy.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the labor market tightening condition does not correlate with subsequent economic strength.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the economic expansion condition does not correlate with subsequent equity performance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as higher borrowing costs weigh on corporate earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or FEDFUNDS increase does not correlate with subsequent earnings contraction.
